name: Nebraska veterans: county veterans service officers for claims help
organization: County veterans service officers; Nebraska Department of Veterans’ Affairs
description: Free help with VA claims, pension and survivor benefits, Nebraska Veterans Aid applications and other benefits from county veterans service officers. Every county has one; some officers serve two to four neighboring counties and keep part-week hours. The Nebraska Department of Veterans’ Affairs’ State Service Office in Lincoln also files claims.
next_step: Choose your county for its service officer, address and hours, and call before you go. The NDVA State Service Office is at 402-420-4021.
constraints: Many rural offices are open one to three days a week; check the hours on the county card.

name: Nebraska Aging and Disability Resource Center
organization: Nebraska DHHS State Unit on Aging and the Area Agencies on Aging
description: Nebraska’s Aging and Disability Resource Centers give information, referrals and help with community services and long-term care options to people 60 and older, people with disabilities of any age, and their families and caregivers. The Area Agencies on Aging run the local centers. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 844-843-6364, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (Nebraska SHIP) for Nebraska
organization: Nebraska Department of Insurance, State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) and Senior Medicare Patrol (SMP)
description: Free Medicare counseling from Nebraska SHIP, a division of the Nebraska Department of Insurance that does not sell insurance or endorse any company: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help paying for Medicare. Its Senior Medicare Patrol helps people report Medicare fraud and errors.
next_step: Call 800-234-7119 to reach a counselor or arrange a meeting. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

name: Nebraska Long-Term Care Ombudsman and abuse reporting
organization: Nebraska Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
description: Independent advocacy for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, through regional ombudsmen and the state office in Lincoln.
next_step: Call the state ombudsman office at 402-802-5541. To report abuse or neglect of a vulnerable adult, call 800-652-1999. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: Free legal help for Nebraska veterans and older adults
description: Legal Aid of Nebraska gives free civil legal help to people with low incomes across the state through its AccessLine. Its Elder AccessLine gives Nebraskans 60 and older free legal advice and help, working with the Area Agencies on Aging.
next_step: Call the Legal Aid of Nebraska AccessLine at 877-250-2016. If you are 60 or older, call the Elder AccessLine at 800-527-7249 (402-827-5656 in Omaha).
constraints: The general AccessLine screens by income and case type.

name: VA health care systems serving Nebraska
description: Most Nebraska veterans are served by the VA Nebraska-Western Iowa Health Care System (Omaha VA Medical Center, 4101 Woolworth Avenue; 402-346-8800), with clinics including Lincoln and Grand Island. In the Panhandle, the Scottsbluff clinic is run by the VA Black Hills Health Care System in Hot Springs, South Dakota, and the Sidney clinic by the Cheyenne VA Medical Center.
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

name: Independence Rising (central and western Nebraska)
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.

The phone is the Grand Island office (3335 West Capital Avenue). Other offices: Scottsbluff 308-633-7025; North Platte 308-221-6073; Kearney 308-708-2392; Gothenburg 308-537-4332; McCook and Maxwell 308-258-1914.
